scope.work: V12-T0 control-plane alignment plus CPF-1 source-only persistence-sink inventory

verdict.rule: Any reachable unknown sink keeps CPF-1 incomplete and fail-closed.

sinks.serialization: JSON nativeContract containing the complete OwnerAlphaPracticeSession
sinks.retention: Durable; no TTL or deletion path is established in the repository source.
sinks.redaction: None before raw_payload serialization.
sinks.retry: User commands re-save the complete session; provider timeout state is itself persisted.
sinks.failure: Repository errors surface to the route; a failed provider attempt may leave a durable failed session state.
sinks.verdict: D1-D3 persistence violates the zero-retention contract; D4 also lacks the required scrub.

sinks.serialization: answerText or rewriteText in raw_payload; derived_payload also sets containsRawContent=false
sinks.retention: Durable; no TTL is specified.
sinks.redaction: No learner-body scrub is applied.
sinks.retry: Repeated user save can create or update durable records.
sinks.failure: Database errors are returned as generic route failures; raw-content attestation remains declarative.
sinks.verdict: D4 is persisted without the mandatory scrub and containsRawContent=false is not evidence of absence.

sinks.serialization: raw_question_text, raw_answer_text, correct_answer, user_answer and raw_payload; derived_payload says containsRawContent=false
sinks.sink: PostgreSQL wrong_answer_items, review_queue_items, action_seeds and usage_events
sinks.retention: Durable; no source-class TTL.
sinks.redaction: sanitizeDerivedMetadata is key-name based and does not scrub the raw columns or arbitrary allowed-key values.
sinks.retry: Completion can be invoked again; repository-level writes are not an atomic source-safety projection.
sinks.failure: Partial multi-table persistence is possible; errors can leave an incomplete projection.
sinks.verdict: D1 and D3 are stored directly and the boolean attestation contradicts the serialized bodies.

sinks.serialization: Free strings from problemSummary, concepts, formulas, commonMistakes and nextPracticeAction become derived_tags/related_formulas/next_task
sinks.retention: Durable; no TTL.
sinks.redaction: Key-based metadata sanitizer only; no value classifier or closed-code allowlist covers these free strings.
sinks.retry: Client local outbox retains the full generated result after a failed save and the user can retry.
sinks.failure: A failed save diverts D1-D3 to browser localStorage; a successful save can durably retain the same classes.
sinks.verdict: The route labels arbitrary source-bound text as a durable learning signal.

sinks.serialization: Heuristically filtered provider-derived strings plus bodyless usage metadata
sinks.retention: Durable; no TTL.
sinks.redaction: String heuristics and key-name filtering, not a D0-D6 value-level classifier.
sinks.retry: A manual retry re-sends source and may persist another signal/usage event.
sinks.failure: Usage failure is logged separately; derived free text can still cross the boundary.
sinks.verdict: D5/D6 are intended, but D2/D3 exclusion is not proven.

sinks.serialization: answer, transcription, provider scores, weaknesses and next_action
sinks.sink: PostgreSQL evaluations, daily_missions and analytics summary
sinks.retention: Durable; no TTL or source-class deletion behavior.
sinks.redaction: None for answer/transcription; UUID validation only controls whether the write runs.
sinks.retry: Manual request retry repeats provider processing and database write.
sinks.failure: Repository catches and suppresses all save errors, so the response cannot prove whether persistence occurred.
sinks.verdict: D1/D3/D4 are durably stored; D4 is not scrubbed.

sinks.serialization: Plain SHA-256 learner-input fingerprint, review identity, revisions, findings, evidence and transitions
sinks.sink: PostgreSQL s233a review records, concept transitions, review queue and action seeds
sinks.retention: Durable immutable/revision records; no fingerprint rotation window.
sinks.redaction: Bodies are mostly excluded, but the content-derived SHA-256 is stable and unkeyed.
sinks.retry: Retryable failures and retry claims are persisted against the same fingerprint.
sinks.failure: failed_retryable is durable failure recovery metadata.
sinks.verdict: Durable closed evidence is intended, but an unkeyed raw-content fingerprint is forbidden D2.

sinks.entry: Review OS notes, feedback, study logs, review queue, action seeds and wrong-answer APIs
sinks.serialization: Free-text route/page/message, source labels, note text, rendered text and raw_payload
sinks.sink: PostgreSQL feedback_items, study_logs, review_queue_items, action_seeds, wrong_answer_items and related tables
sinks.retention: Durable; table-specific TTL is not present in source.
sinks.redaction: Derived metadata is key-filtered; learner free text is not scrubbed by class.
sinks.retry: Route or client retries can duplicate or overwrite records depending on adapter.
sinks.failure: Several service methods console.warn error objects and return fallback states.
sinks.verdict: D4/D5/D6 share broad adapters; the closed-projection boundary is not enforced.

sinks.entry: Second-exam submission and rewrite API routes
sinks.serialization: Learner answer/rewrite bodies and workflow metadata
sinks.retention: Durable; no scrub/TTL contract in the adapter.
sinks.redaction: No D4 scrub before raw_payload.
sinks.retry: Manual retries may repeat inserts/updates.
sinks.failure: When Supabase is unavailable or unconfigured, the implementation can use the local JSON fallback.
sinks.verdict: D4 is persisted without the contractually required scrub.

sinks.entry: Second-exam submission/rewrite APIs when the database adapter is unavailable
sinks.serialization: Pretty-printed JSON
sinks.retention: Process/filesystem lifetime; no TTL, encryption or cleanup.
sinks.redaction: None.
sinks.retry: Synchronous file lock retries 200 times at 10 ms.
sinks.failure: Parse failure silently replaces the store with a seed; stale lock directories can survive a crash.
sinks.verdict: D4 is stored in an unscoped local artifact and fallback tenant isolation is not proven.

sinks.serialization: JSON event envelope with arbitrary properties values after key-based sanitization
sinks.retention: Latest 1000 records; count cap only, no time TTL.
sinks.redaction: sanitizeDerivedMetadata removes suspicious keys but not source text placed under allowed keys.
sinks.retry: sendBeacon falls back to keepalive fetch; browser may retry only through caller behavior.
sinks.failure: Client failures are swallowed or debug-logged; server failure returns event-persistence-error.
sinks.verdict: Intended D5/D6 telemetry can carry D2/D3 because value-level enforcement is absent.

sinks.serialization: FeedbackResponse including freeText and learner context
sinks.retention: Latest 500 records; no time TTL.
sinks.redaction: No free-text scrub.
sinks.retry: Client retry can append another response.
sinks.failure: Persistence errors return a generic code; GET exposes the accumulated records without an auth check in this route.
sinks.verdict: Learner-authored D4 is durably stored and exposed through a broad admin-like surface.

sinks.serialization: Full AI input/output/meta JSON
sinks.retention: Latest 500 records; no time TTL or encryption.
sinks.redaction: No D-class projection before the admin record.
sinks.retry: Manual retry can generate and store another full item.
sinks.failure: Provider failure falls back or returns generic handling; persisted review data is not covered by a zero-write receipt.
sinks.verdict: Full provider/learner-derived bodies are retained in an admin artifact.

sinks.entry: Any createJsonFileRepository write carrying source-bound or learner bodies
sinks.serialization: Complete JSON snapshot
sinks.retention: Normally milliseconds until rename/removal; crash residue has no cleanup ceiling.
sinks.redaction: None.
sinks.retry: Lock acquisition retries for up to about 2 seconds.
sinks.failure: A process crash can leave a complete .tmp file or lock directory.
sinks.verdict: The temporary path is still a filesystem persistence sink and violates zero disk-spill for D1-D3.

sinks.serialization: Gemini generateContent prompt plus inline base64 file bytes; full response JSON/text
sinks.sink: Gemini request handling, provider logs/cache/abuse review and response systems
sinks.retention: Repository supplies no verified zero-content-retention binding; live account settings were not called.
sinks.redaction: No on-device OCR/minimization; original bytes and confirmed text are sent.
sinks.retry: User can retry; 25 s Promise.race timeout does not abort the underlying provider request.
sinks.failure: Timed-out provider work can continue after the application returns and its retention outcome is unknown.
sinks.verdict: Reachable D0-D4 provider sink is fail-closed unknown and currently lacks the required exact route controls.

sinks.serialization: Multipart text/file bytes converted to provider prompt/inline data
sinks.retention: Unknown from repository source and live settings were forbidden.
sinks.redaction: No source-class minimization contract.
sinks.retry: Manual retry; no explicit abort deadline.
sinks.failure: No zero-write receipt and no explicit provider deletion behavior.
sinks.verdict: Full source travels to a provider route whose retention/caching state is unknown.

sinks.serialization: Text prompts and inline image/file bytes; one or two provider calls per request
sinks.retention: No repository proof of zero retention, prompt-cache disablement, region or human-review controls.
sinks.redaction: No on-device OCR or value-level minimization is enforced.
sinks.retry: Manual retry; some flows make a second provider call by design and have no abort control.
sinks.failure: Provider errors become generic responses or sanitized codes, but provider-side residue is unverified.
sinks.verdict: D0/D1/D4 provider egress is reachable and fail-closed unknown.

sinks.serialization: Chat/completion request and response bodies
sinks.retention: No exact organization/project/endpoint/store=false evidence in repository; live settings were not called.
sinks.redaction: No D4 scrub before provider egress.
sinks.retry: Manual retry; AI-assist has an application timeout but provider storage controls are not explicit.
sinks.failure: Fallback/mock paths do not prove deletion of an already accepted provider request.
sinks.verdict: Reachable provider boundary remains unknown and blocks CPF-1 completion.

sinks.serialization: JSON.stringify of the complete result
sinks.retention: Indefinite until explicit browser/user removal; no TTL, encryption or item cap is established.
sinks.redaction: None.
sinks.retry: The retained result is intended for later retry.
sinks.failure: The failure path itself creates persistent D1-D3 residue.
sinks.verdict: A durable browser retry sink stores the full source-bound output.

sinks.entry: Problem Snap bridge to Answer Review
sinks.serialization: JSON result/handoff object
sinks.retention: Tab/session lifetime until the consumer removes it; crash/navigation residue is browser-defined.
sinks.redaction: None.
sinks.retry: Not a retry queue, but it survives navigation in the same tab.
sinks.failure: If the consumer never runs, the full handoff remains for the session.
sinks.verdict: Transient browser persistence still carries prohibited D1-D3.

sinks.entry: Review OS draft and local-beta note UI
sinks.serialization: Generic JSON or free problemTitle/biggestGap/nextAction strings
sinks.retention: Indefinite until clear action; local notes capped at 20 but have no TTL.
sinks.redaction: Generic drafts have none; local-note key allowlist does not classify string values.
sinks.retry: Storage errors are swallowed.
sinks.failure: metadataOnly=true is declarative and does not prevent source expression in allowed fields.
sinks.verdict: Generic and free-text browser persistence has no D0-D6 enforcement.

sinks.entry: Learner autosave and subject drafting surfaces
sinks.serialization: Generic draft JSON and SubjectDraft JSON
sinks.retention: Indefinite until explicit clear; savedAt is informational only.
sinks.redaction: None; generic type parameters accept arbitrary bodies.
sinks.retry: 700 ms autosave retries only on subsequent state changes; errors become UI status.
sinks.failure: Quota/storage failure does not erase prior source-bearing drafts.
sinks.verdict: Learner/source bodies can persist without TTL, encryption or class validation.

sinks.entry: Client event, feedback and calculator outbox flows
sinks.serialization: Event envelopes, anonymous ID, prompt state, feedback responses and queued actions
sinks.sink: inverge:events:*, inverge:feedback:* and local outbox keys
sinks.retention: Events/counts are capped in some paths; no common TTL or encryption.
sinks.redaction: Event sanitizer is key-based; calculator outbox is closed-key validated; feedback freeText is unredacted.
sinks.retry: sendBeacon falls back to fetch and outboxes retry later.
sinks.failure: Failure can extend browser retention and error details may be debug-logged outside production.
sinks.verdict: D5/D6 paths are mixed with unvalidated D2/D4 values.

sinks.entry: Multipart/JSON request routes and React client state
sinks.service: Next Request.formData/json, File.arrayBuffer and provider adapters
sinks.serialization: File/Uint8Array/base64/string/JSON objects
sinks.sink: Request buffers, React state, provider SDK objects and response buffers
sinks.retention: Request/process/GC lifetime; no enforceable 600 s hard ceiling is implemented.
sinks.redaction: Generally none before provider serialization.
sinks.retry: Manual retry recreates buffers; provider timeouts may leave in-flight SDK objects.
sinks.failure: Unhandled/runtime/platform behavior can copy memory into crash or diagnostic systems.
sinks.verdict: Transient by application design, but the hard ceiling and downstream crash boundary are unproven.

sinks.entry: Rate limit, client event dedupe and development learning metrics
sinks.serialization: Keys, timestamps and closed counters
sinks.retention: Process lifetime with implementation-specific pruning.
sinks.redaction: Designed as bodyless/closed metadata; source value injection was not found in these adapters.
sinks.retry: No durable retry.
sinks.failure: Restart loses state; no disk or shared-cache adapter was found.
sinks.verdict: No current D0-D4 content cache adapter found; platform/shared-cache settings remain unknown.

sinks.entry: OCR, answer-review and Problem Snap route completion/failure
sinks.serialization: event name, hashed user ID, route, mode, subject, cost category, duration, status and sanitized error code
sinks.sink: Runtime stdout and hosting log pipeline
sinks.retention: Application source does not control log retention.
sinks.redaction: Bodyless fixed fields; user ID is truncated SHA-256 and error code is character/length constrained.
sinks.retry: Each route execution logs once; hosting delivery retries are unknown.
sinks.failure: The application shape is bodyless, but downstream log copies/backups are platform-controlled.
sinks.verdict: Application payload is D6; actual log retention and downstream copies remain unknown.

sinks.entry: Review OS and client persistence/provider error paths
sinks.serialization: JavaScript Error or provider/database error objects
sinks.sink: Browser developer console and runtime/hosting logs
sinks.retention: Browser and platform defined.
sinks.redaction: No central error-object redactor is applied; some route errors use safe codes, others pass objects.
sinks.retry: Repeated failures repeat logging.
sinks.failure: SDK errors may embed request/provider context even when source code does not intentionally log bodies.
sinks.verdict: Reachable error-reporting sink has unproven value-level redaction.

sinks.service: Next.js route runtime, proxy/edge and hosting platform
sinks.serialization: HTTP multipart/JSON request and JSON response bodies
sinks.sink: Request buffering, temporary disk, CDN/response cache, logs, traces, APM, crash reports, session replay, snapshots and support systems
sinks.retention: Not established by repository source; dynamic routes do not prove no-store for every response and no live platform query was allowed.
sinks.redaction: No end-to-end platform configuration evidence.
sinks.retry: Client, proxy and platform retry behavior is unverified.
sinks.failure: Timeout/crash paths may retain diagnostic copies.
sinks.verdict: Reachable unknown sink family; CPF-1 cannot complete.

sinks.redaction: Copies inherit persisted row contents.

confirmedViolations.finding: exam_sessions.raw_payload stores the complete OwnerAlphaPracticeSession, including D1-D4 and full provider output.
containsRawContent=false coexists with raw_question_text/raw_answer_text/correct_answer/raw_payload; it is a declaration, not proof.
/problem-snap/save persists arbitrary provider/source-derived strings as learning_signal_events without a value classifier.
Problem Snap save failure and handoff persist D1-D3 in localStorage/sessionStorage.
Generic Review OS, learner autosave and subject draft helpers persist arbitrary bodies without TTL/encryption/class enforcement.
The evaluate flow persists learner answer, transcription and provider output in Supabase and silently suppresses write failures.
Second-exam database and JSON fallback paths persist unscreened D4; the fallback also creates .tmp residue.
Gemini routes send original bytes/text without repository proof of exact zero-retention, no-cache and account bindings.
OpenAI routes do not establish exact organization/project/endpoint/store=false retention controls in source.
Second-exam AI assist persists full provider input/output to an admin JSON file.
S233A uses a stable unkeyed SHA-256 of private learner input as durable retry/identity material.
Telemetry sanitization is key-name based and permits source text under allowed property keys.
Feedback free text is persisted to a JSON artifact and the same route exposes aggregate GET without an auth gate.
The JSON fallback has no TTL/encryption, can leave crash residue, and resets to seed on parse failure.
Owner-alpha provider timeout uses Promise.race without aborting the underlying provider call.
D4 scrub_required is not implemented consistently before database, file, browser or provider persistence.

cpf2aProposedChangeSurface: Introduce value-level D0-D6 ingress classification and typed closed projections; remove reliance on containsRawContent booleans.
Create a no-database/no-storage/no-disk/no-analytics ephemeral processor and deny source routes all durable credentials.
Move OCR/minimization on-device where possible and transmit only the minimum confirmed fields.
Bind provider adapters to exact organization/project/endpoint/model with verified zero-content retention, store=false, cache disabled, abortable deadlines and a drift kill switch.
Add no-store/private response headers and tests across every source-bearing route.
Stop D0-D3 writes to exam_sessions, wrong_answer_items, learning_signal_events, evaluations, JSON fallbacks, admin artifacts and browser storage.
Implement a documented D4 scrub plus closed D5/D6 allowlists before any database, telemetry, queue, log or browser sink.
Replace stable raw-content SHA-256 identifiers with short-lived rotating keyed HMAC used only for abuse protection, never retrieval.
Centralize error-object redaction and prove request/response bodies are absent from logging, tracing, crash, replay and support systems.
Add zero-write receipts, hostile canaries and failure/timeout/retry residue tests before any real-content authorization.
migrationImplications: Existing rows/artifacts may already contain D1-D4 and require a separately authorized inventory, quarantine, deletion/backfill and backup-propagation plan.
Disabling future writes can be done before schema removal, but column removal, constraints, RLS changes and data cleanup require explicit migration authority.
Browser keys need a versioned purge/migration path; silent retention is not acceptable.
File fallback data and crash residue require an exact deployment-filesystem cleanup plan.
Provider and managed-service deletion evidence must account for backups, abuse-monitoring exceptions and contractual retention.
No migration, cleanup or live read is authorized by this inventory PR.
